deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no derivation. It is an outline of three section headings in German, with a few Latin vocabulary notes below. The headings match the structure of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (Göttingen 1851). The neighbouring pages are draft or fair-copy text of that dissertation. The previous page is the mean-value formula u_0 = (1/2π)∮(log r ∂u/∂p − u ∂log r/∂p) ds = (1/2π)∫_0^{2π} u dφ and the regularity / removable-singularity theorem for harmonic functions (dissertation Art. 9–11). The next page is the 'Zusatz zu pag. 1' giving the ε–α definition of continuity.

The three headings are:

(I) 'Über die Definition einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. This corresponds to dissertation Art. 1–4: the definition of a complex function by complex differentiability, dw/dz independent of direction, i.e. the Cauchy–Riemann equations.

(II) 'Über die Bedingungen, unter welchen eine Function einer innerhalb eines begrenzten Grössengebiets veränderlichen complexen Grösse im Innern desselben überall endlich und stetig ist'. This corresponds to the theorem on the preceding page and dissertation Art. 11–12. Under mild hypotheses (exceptional points fill no area, discontinuities fill no line, ρ·∂u/∂x → 0 at isolated singular points, no removable discontinuity in u), a harmonic function or complex function is finite and continuous together with all its derivatives. This is essentially the removable-singularity theorem. The words 'innerhalb desselben' were struck and replaced by 'im Innern desselben'.

(III) 'Über die Determination einer Function einer innerhalb eines gegebenen [abgegrenzten?] Grössengebiets von 2 Dimensionen veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. This corresponds to dissertation Art. 16–18: determination of the function by boundary data and discontinuities via the Dirichlet principle, i.e. minimising ∫∫((∂α/∂x−∂β/∂y)²+(∂α/∂y+∂β/∂x)²) dT.

Below the headings are Latin terminology notes: 'propositio', 'antecedens — Voraussetzung', 'consequens — Folge', 'Propositiones', 'sequenter notamus' (partly struck), and 'I. De definitione'. These suggest Riemann was preparing a Latin rendering of the dissertation's contents, perhaps for the theses or Latin formalities connected with the 1851 promotion. He is fixing Latin equivalents for 'hypothesis' and 'conclusion' and beginning a Latin section 'I. De definitione [functionis…]'. 'Riemann 13' at the top is an archival or bundle annotation. The '20' in the right margin is the folio number.

results.what: Outline of the three main topics of Riemann's 1851 dissertation: definition of a complex function, conditions for finiteness/continuity (removable singularities), and determination of a function in a bounded 2-dimensional domain (Dirichlet principle)
results.modern_name: Structure of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation (complex differentiability / Cauchy–Riemann definition; Riemann removable singularity theorem; Dirichlet principle / boundary value determination)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a table-of-contents style outline of Riemann's well-known 1851 dissertation plus Latin vocabulary notes. Its only interest is documentary: it hints at a planned Latin rendering. It contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Context from the previous page used for heading II: log r is harmonic away from O_0, which underlies the integral representation and the regularity theorem.
Mean-value property (previous-page formula u_0=(1/2π)∫u dφ) for the sample harmonic function Re(z^2+3) at the origin.

transcription_corrections: Heading III: 'innerhalb eines begrenzten [?] einen Grössengebiets' should be a single phrase, most likely 'innerhalb eines gegebenen (or abgegrenzten) Grössengebiets'. The doubled 'begrenzten … einen' is a transcription artefact.
'Propositiones sequentes [?] notamus [?]' reads more like 'sequenter notamus', with 'notamus' apparently struck through.
Heading II: the struck words read 'innerhalb desselben', replaced by 'im Innern desselben'; the transcription's markup is correct.
The small '20' in the right margin (folio number) is omitted by the transcription; 'Riemann 13' is an archival annotation, not Riemann's text.
